scope: H2 replay scheduling. TileBinReplayScheduler distributes completed per-tile chains from TileBinDirectory across two independently progressing PrimitiveBinReader engines sharing one tagged memory port. This is not a primitive/state handle cache, cache-domain integration, spill policy, downstream tile engine or full binner replacement, and it is not integrated into RenderPipeline yet.

configuration.memory_client: one tagged 64-byte read port with an RRArbiter; one outstanding line per engine
configuration.job_input: TileBinCompletion from TileBinDirectory.tileClosed (identity, tile, status, prefixUsable, head, committedCount, restart)

scheduler_contract.dispatch: Completed tiles enter per-engine two-entry queues in rotating order; each engine starts its buffered job as soon as its reader is free.
scheduler_contract.independence: Each engine has its own PrimitiveBinReader, reference stream, completion register and error status. A fault or output stall on one engine does not stop the other from fetching and replaying.
scheduler_contract.ordering: Per-engine reference and completion order is preserved; the reference ordinal is the exact per-tile ordinal from replay.
scheduler_contract.unusable_tiles: Tiles with no usable prefix or no head complete without memory traffic and retain the directory status; an empty successful chain reports success with zero emitted.
scheduler_contract.status: A replay error overrides the directory status; otherwise exhausted or success is retained. A memory fault dominates the pass summary.
scheduler_contract.cancel: Cancellation stops dispatch, drains every started reader (offered references still leave that engine), reports buffered jobs cancelled, and auto-completes the summary once the engines are empty.
scheduler_contract.end: End is accepted only after every queue and reader is idle and every per-tile completion has been consumed; the summary then reports tiles, references, pages and read lines.
scheduler_contract.integration_limit: The caller must keep the arena owned through the summary, publish directory stores to the replay memory domain, and drain every per-tile completion.

coverage: Two tile chains replay concurrently on separate engines; both engines are busy in the same cycle, each stream reports its own tile and the per-tile ordinals and references match the stored image (6 references and 1 page per tile).
Four tiles are accepted behind two running jobs through the two-entry engine queues; each engine processes two tiles and all 12 references replay.
Empty and unusable tiles complete without any memory request, retain their status, and the invalid-order status reaches the pass summary.
A faulted header line on one engine reports memoryFault with an unusable prefix while the other engine replays its five references and reports success.
Cancellation with reads outstanding drains started readers, reports all buffered jobs cancelled, leaves no pending read, and completes the summary as cancelled.
Per-engine output backpressure across nine references and three pages per tile preserves per-tile order and ordinals on both engines.
functional.cycle_scope: Cycles include scripted read latency, request stalls and per-engine completion handshakes. These are control-component workloads, not a full-frame or product-bandwidth result.
functional.proof_limit: Numeric/protocol simulation with per-engine references checked against independent images; no universal temporal formal proof.

timing.first_synthesis: The scheduler passed synthesis on its first attempt at +31.578 ps (1032.608 MHz); no retiming change was required.
timing.route: The closure run with 30 ps repair margin reaches +40.6475 ps setup and +24.0397 ps hold at 1042.37 MHz.

qualification.scope: All reported synthesis setup paths, including I/O

mapping.scope: Synthesis mapping report; omitted operators and undriven logic fail qualification

qualification.scope: Post-route global setup/hold including I/O; placement, DRC, antenna and flow errors

critical_path.startpoint: u4821 (rising edge-triggered flip-flop clocked by core_clock)
critical_path.endpoint: u14407 (rising edge-triggered flip-flop clocked by core_clock)

remaining: Wire TileBinDirectory into the scheduler and the scheduler into a tile-engine consumer, add primitive/state handle fetch and cache, cache-domain publication, a full spill/restart policy, load balancing/fairness measurements, attachment-bytes/frame and realistic bandwidth/product-frame measurements.
